📌 INTRODUCTION
The YAJIB Educational Video Creator Studio is a powerful, browser-based tool that allows educators, trainers, and content creators to:

🎥 Record video lectures with screen capture and camera overlay

🎙️ Add voice-over narration to existing videos

✏️ Annotate and draw on screen in real-time

🖼️ Insert images for demonstration purposes

📹 Float your camera as a Picture-in-Picture (PiP) overlay

💾 Export recordings in multiple formats

Key Advantage: Everything runs in your browser - no software installation required!

🚀 GETTING STARTED
1. Access the Application
Simply open the index.html file in a modern browser:

Chrome 86+ (recommended)

Edge 86+

Firefox 80+

Safari 15+

2. Grant Permissions
When you first open the app, your browser will ask for:

Permission	Purpose
📷 Camera	For the floating presenter overlay (PiP)
🎙️ Microphone	For recording voice and audio
🖥️ Screen Share	For recording your screen/lecture
How to allow:

Click "Allow" when prompted

If you missed it, click the camera/mic icon in your browser's address bar

3. Understand the Interface

📝 STEP-BY-STEP TUTORIALS
🎓 Tutorial 1: Recording a Lecture (Screen + Camera)
Goal: Record your screen with your face visible as a floating overlay.

Step 1: Select Lecture Mode
Click the "🎓 Lecture Recording" button at the top

Step 2: Verify Your Camera is Working
Look for the floating presenter window (usually bottom-right)

If you don't see it, check camera permissions

Step 3: Prepare Your Screen
Open any application, presentation, or content you want to record

Arrange windows for optimal viewing

Step 4: Start Recording
Click the Red "Start Recording" button

When prompted, select which screen/window to share

Choose your entire screen or a specific application

Click "Share" or "Allow"

Step 5: Interact with Your Content
Navigate through your presentation normally

Annotate using the tools (see Tutorial 3)

Insert images for demonstration (see Tutorial 4)

Your floating camera will follow you

Step 6: Control Recording
⏸️ Pause - Temporarily stop recording (click Pause)

▶️ Resume - Click the recording button again

⏹️ Stop - End recording and save

Step 7: Export Your Lecture
Click "Export MP4" or "Export WebM"

Your video will download automatically

The file will be named with the recording timestamp

🎙️ Tutorial 2: Voice-Over for Existing Videos
Goal: Add professional voice-over narration to an existing video.

Step 1: Switch to Voice-Over Mode
Click "🎙️ Voice-Over" mode button

Step 2: Paste Your Video Link
In the Voice-Over section, paste a video URL (e.g., YouTube link)

OR paste a direct link to an MP4 file

Click "Load Video"

Step 3: Preview the Video
The video will appear in the main canvas

Use the video controls to preview and position

Step 4: Start Voice Recording
Click the Red "Start Recording" button

The video will start playing automatically

Speak your narration into your microphone

Step 5: Sync Your Voice
The recording captures both the video playback and your voice

Your floating camera will show you speaking

Step 6: Pause/Resume
⏸️ Pause - Pause both video and recording

▶️ Resume - Continue from where you paused

Step 7: Export
Your recording will include the video + your synchronized voice-over

Export as MP4 or WebM

✏️ Tutorial 3: Using Annotation Tools
Goal: Add drawings, highlights, and text to your recordings.

3.1 Pen Tool
Click the "Pen" button in the tools panel

Choose your color from the 🎨 Color Picker

Click and drag on the canvas to draw

Lines appear in real-time

Use Cases:

Underline important points

Draw diagrams

Circle key information

Write equations

3.2 Highlighter Tool
Click "Highlight" button

Drag over text to highlight (semi-transparent)

Use a bright color for visibility

Use Cases:

Emphasize key phrases

Mark important passages

Draw attention to specific areas

3.3 Text Tool
Click "Text" button

Click anywhere on the canvas

Type your text

Use Cases:

Add titles and labels

Write quick notes

Display key points

3.4 Shape Tool
Click "Shape" button

Draw rectangles, circles, or arrows

Click and drag to create shapes

Use Cases:

Create boxes around content

Draw arrows to point to things

Highlight sections with rectangles

3.5 Clear All
Click "Clear All" to remove all annotations

Great for starting fresh

🖼️ Tutorial 4: Inserting Images for Demonstration
Goal: Add images during recording for visual demonstrations.

Step 1: Click Insert Image
Click the "Insert Image" button in the tools panel

Step 2: Select Your Image
Choose an image file (PNG, JPG, SVG, GIF)

The image appears on the canvas

Step 3: Position the Image
The image is placed at the default position

You can drag it around (future enhancement)

Use Cases:

Show product photos

Display diagrams

Demonstrate software screenshots

Show before/after comparisons

🎬 Tutorial 5: Using the Floating Presenter (PiP)
Goal: Position and customize your camera overlay.

5.1 Move the PiP
Click and drag the PiP window anywhere on screen

It floats above ALL content

5.2 Resize the PiP
Use the size presets in the sidebar:

S = Small (160px)

M = Medium (220px) - Default

L = Large (300px)

XL = Extra Large (380px)

Or drag the bottom-right corner to resize manually

5.3 Control the PiP
👁️ Toggle Visibility - Show or hide the PiP

🎙️ Mute/Unmute - Control microphone

↕️ Reset Position - Return to bottom-right corner

5.4 PiP Tips
Position PiP in a corner to avoid blocking content

Use Medium size for most lectures

Use Small size when showing detailed content

Mute to avoid audio feedback during playback

💡 TIPS & BEST PRACTICES
🎬 Recording Tips
Prepare Your Content

Have your slides/presentation ready

Practice your narration beforehand

Know what you want to annotate

Environment Setup

Quiet room for recording

Good lighting for camera

Close unnecessary applications

PiP Placement

Place in top-right or bottom-right corner

Avoid covering important content

Use small size if showing detailed information

Audio Quality

Use a good microphone

Test audio levels before recording

Minimize background noise

Recording Length

Keep lectures focused (15-30 minutes)

Use Pause for breaks

Split long content into multiple recordings

✏️ Annotation Best Practices
Use Contrasting Colors: Yellow highlights on dark text, dark pen on light backgrounds

Be Deliberate: Annotate purposefully, not excessively

Plan Annotations: Know what you'll highlight before recording

Clear Before Moving: Use "Clear All" when switching topics

🎯 Voice-Over Tips
Script Your Narration: Prepare what you'll say

Speak Clearly: Enunciate for better audio capture

Pause Naturally: Allow time for video content to be seen

Sync Cue Points: Time your narration with key video moments

🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING
Common Issues & Solutions
Issue	Likely Cause	Solution
Camera not showing	Permission denied	Grant camera permission in browser
No microphone audio	Microphone blocked	Check browser permissions
Screen sharing fails	Browser security	Use Chrome or Edge
Recording button doesn't work	Missing permissions	Refresh and re-allow permissions
Video won't load (Voice-Over)	Invalid URL or CORS	Use direct video file URLs
No recording saved	Recording stopped improperly	Check stop button, try again
PiP won't drag	Touch/mouse conflict	Click once to select, then drag
Annotations not showing	Not in recording mode	Start recording first
Browser-Specific Issues
Chrome/Edge:

Best performance overall

Recommended browser

Firefox:

Some advanced features may have limited support

Safari:

Limited screen sharing support

Use Chrome for best experience

Quick Fixes
Refresh the page - Most issues resolved

Re-grant permissions - Click the 🔒 icon in address bar

Check console - Open F12 to see any errors

Use incognito/private mode - Bypass extension conflicts

Update browser - Use latest version
